evidence_completeness.evidence: The reviewer artifact systematically addresses the task's two parts: provenance facts represented and questions outside specification. Part 1 verifies specific facts (Identity, Integrity, Lineage, VEX, AI Profile) with references to SPDX 3.0.1 and CycloneDX v1.7 specifications. Part 2 explicitly details boundaries/exclusions for both specs. Part 3 lists 10 specific supply-chain questions outside the specs, categorized by gap type (semantic, spec boundary, practical). Each claim is backed by traceable references to specification sections or external standards (SLSA, SCITT). The artifact clearly distinguishes between what the specs define versus what requires external mechanisms.

citation_quality.evidence: The artifact provides a comprehensive 'Sources' section with 11 specific references. These include primary specification links (SPDX 3.0.1 Scope, Build Profile, AI Profile, SPDX 2.3 Composition; ECMA-424 CycloneDX v1.7) and relevant external standards/academic papers (Rasheed et al., IETF SCITT). The citations are directly linked to the claims they support in the text (e.g., referencing SPDX §5.3 for exclusions, CycloneDX use cases for pedigree). All cited URLs appear valid and accessible structure-wise (GitHub, ECMA, CycloneDX domains).

contradiction_handling.evidence: The artifact explicitly handles the nuance between 'hosting' references to attestation and 'providing' attestation. It clarifies that while both specs can reference SLSA/in-toto, neither is an attestation framework itself. It also distinguishes between AI package provenance (in scope) and AI-generated code provenance (out of scope). The gap analysis categorizes conflicts or absences as 'semantic', 'spec boundary', or 'practical' rather than errors, accurately reconciling the descriptive nature of BOMs with the cryptographic needs of trust.
